title: Key verbs: give, keep and miss
subtitle: give me a hand, keep quiet, miss a chance
summary: Learn the everyday phrases built from three key verbs: give, keep and miss.

lesson.heading: give = cause an effect
lesson.text: We use **give** when someone or something causes a certain effect in another person.

examples.text: All that noise has **given** me a headache.
The walk this morning **gave** me an appetite.
Listening to Wai Sin has **given** me an idea.
Valentina **gave** us a shock when she shouted like that.

lesson.heading: give + noun = an action
rows: talk formally to a group of people
I had to give a speech at the wedding.
Ollie gave me a hand with my work.
He gave the car a push.

lesson.heading: keep = stay in a state
lesson.text: **Keep** can mean to stay, or to cause someone to stay, in a particular state or condition. It is followed by an adjective.

examples.text: I never drink coffee at night; it **keeps** me **awake**.

lesson.heading: keep (on) doing something
lesson.text: **Keep** or **keep on** + *-ing* means to repeat doing something. Often it is something you do not want to do or to happen.

examples.note: = disturbs me when I am doing something

examples.text: I **keep waking** up early because it's so light in my bedroom.

lesson.heading: keep in touch, keep a secret, keep it up
lesson.text: If you **keep in touch**, you continue to communicate with someone. If you **keep a secret**, you don't tell other people. If you **keep it up**, you continue doing something at a high level.

examples.text: I met Mara on holiday and we've **kept in touch** ever since.
Tom told me not to tell anyone, but I'm not very good at **keeping a secret**.
Your English is improving. That's good - **keep it up**.

lesson.heading: Four meanings of miss
rows: feel sad because a person is not there
When I went to work in Hungary, I really missed my girlfriend.
I'm sorry, I missed that. What did you say?
not use a chance or opportunity
She's injured, so she might miss her chance to play.
I left home early in order to miss the rush hour.

lesson.text: Remember the difference: you **give** someone a hand (= help them), and you **keep** in touch (= go on writing or phoning).

exercises.prompt: Which verb goes with each phrase: give, miss or keep?
Take this umbrella. It should keep you ___.
exercises.explanation: Keep + adjective = stay in that state.

exercises.prompt: They're making a lot of noise in there. Could you tell them to keep ___?
I don't know why she keeps ___ - it wasn't a very funny story.
exercises.explanation: Keep (on) + -ing means to repeat doing something.

exercises.prompt: It's really stupid, but I keep ___ to lock the doors and windows when I go out.
exercises.explanation: Keep + -ing = do it again and again.

exercises.prompt: Match each phrase with give to its meaning.
*A:* He didn't put his arms round her, did he? *B:* Yes. He ___ big hug.
exercises.explanation: Give someone a hug = put your arms round them.

exercises.prompt: *A:* Have you stayed in contact with your old school friends? *B:* Yes, I've tried to ___ as much as possible.
exercises.explanation: Keep in touch = continue to communicate with someone.

exercises.prompt: *A:* He had a chance to go and he didn't take it. *B:* I know. He ___ opportunity.
exercises.explanation: Miss an opportunity = not use a chance to do something.

exercises.prompt: We left before seven because we wanted to ___ the rush hour.
exercises.explanation: Miss something = manage to avoid it.

exercises.prompt: The guys are working really hard, but I don't know if they can keep it ___.
exercises.explanation: Keep it up = continue doing something at a high level.

exercises.statement: If you keep a secret, you tell other people something that you know.
exercises.explanation: If you keep a secret, you do NOT tell other people something that you know.

exercises.prompt: Put the words in order. The music next door is very loud.
exercises.answer: All that noise has given me a headache.
exercises.explanation: Give is used when something causes an effect: it gave me a headache.
